subject: Audit log extract — legal-hold slice & residency boundary questions
messages:
From: Audrey Li <audrey.li@finvest.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Audit log extract — legal-hold slice & residency boundary questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this. Finvest Legal is preparing a legal hold for a subset of tenant activity and we need to understand Redwood's capabilities and timelines for producing audit/access logs that meet eDiscovery requirements. Quick list of must-haves — can you confirm each?

- Ability to export logs for an explicit date range (start/end) per tenant, filtered by region (EU-only)
- Exports must preserve original event timestamps in UTC and include all available fields (actor, source IP, resource, action, request_id)
- Delivery methods: signed HTTPS download (zip/tar), S3 push, or secure transfer (we prefer S3) — which are supported and typical lead times?
- Chain-of-custody & integrity: manifest with checksum per file (SHA256 or MD5) and a file-level index; can Redwood sign the manifest?
- PII considerations: can logs be exported with PII redacted/hashes on request vs. full raw logs? What's the process?
- Retention of the exported copy on Redwood side during transfer: maximum retention window and deletion attestation after handover
- SLA: production window to generate export (business days) and contact for escalation

Also if you can send a sample manifest and a short playbook describing the export flow (who signs what, where do files land, verification steps), that'd help legal review.

Appreciate a short bulleted response — we may need this on an aggressive timeline.

Thanks,

Audrey Li
Senior Counsel, Finvest Capital
legal@finvest.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Audrey Li <audrey.li@finvest.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit log extract — legal-hold slice & residency boundary questions

Hi Audrey — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise answer to each point plus a few optional controls. Attaching a short playbook and a sample manifest in my next message.

- Date-range, per-tenant, region-filtering: Supported. We can scope exports to tenant + region tag (EU regions only). Please provide tenant ID and the ISO timestamps (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ) for the window.

- Timestamps & fields: Exports are generated from our immutable audit store and include UTC timestamps, request_id, actor_id, resource, action, source_ip (if available), and any auxiliary metadata we retain.

- Delivery methods & lead times:
  * S3 push (recommended): secure, multipart upload to a customer bucket — typical turnaround 2-3 business days for a 30-day slice (depends on volume).
  * Signed HTTPS bundle (tar.gz via pre-signed URL): available for smaller exports; typical 1-3 business days.
  * Managed transfer (ours to your endpoint): we can arrange for an SFTP/managed transfer but that adds onboarding time.

- Chain-of-custody & integrity: We produce a manifest.csv listing files, byte size, and SHA256 checksums. We can provide the manifest signed (PGP signature) on request and include a system-generated export UUID and timestamp.

- PII/redaction: Two modes: raw export (exact logs) or redacted export (PII fields hashed with deterministic HMAC using a key we derive per-export). Redaction is performed at export time; note that hashed values are irreversible without the key. If you need field-level masking (replace with [REDACTED]), that's also available but may remove forensic utility.

- Retention during transfer: Redwood will retain the export for up to 14 days by default to allow verification and re-transmit. We can shorten this window on request. After transfer, we provide a deletion attestation (signed statement + manifest of deletion).

- SLA & escalation: Standard production window is 3-5 business days for typical slices; large (>1TB) exports may take 7-10 business days. For legal holds, we provide a priority queue (expedited) with a 48–72 hour target for small slices if needed — please flag as "legal-hold-expedite". For escalation, contact marissa.cole@redwood.com (Customer Success) and me.

Optional: We can include a minimal chain-of-custody PDF that records the generation timestamp, operator id, checksums, and export UUID.

Next steps: please (1) confirm tenant ID and exact UTC window, (2) preferred delivery method (S3 push preferred), and (3) whether you want raw or redacted exports. I'll then attach the sample manifest and playbook and loop in Engineering to schedule.

Best,

Markus Klein
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Audrey Li <audrey.li@finvest.com>

Subject: Re: Audit log extract — legal-hold slice & residency boundary questions

Thanks, Markus — that's helpful. A couple of clarifications before we lock the order:

1) Chain-of-custody: we need the export manifest to include the original event UTC timestamp, the export generation timestamp, and the internal operator id (or system process id). The PGP-signed manifest is preferred.

2) Export retention: Finvest policy requires that Redwood does NOT keep a copy beyond transfer unless we explicitly request Redwood to hold it for X days. We need a contractual attestation that Redwood will delete its copy within Y days (we'd prefer 7) and provide a signed deletion attestation. Is 7 days feasible?

3) Residency: Dataset should be filtered so that only events originating in EU data centers are included. Please confirm how Redwood determines "EU-origin" for cross-border events (e.g., source IP geolocation vs. tenant residency flag).

4) Timestamp fidelity: we require original timestamps unmodified (UTC). Any time-surgery (e.g., normalization) must be noted in the manifest.

If all good, we will request an expedited S3 push for the following tenant and window:
- Tenant ID: finvest-prod-47
- Window: 2027-04-01T00:00:00Z — 2027-04-30T23:59:59Z

Please confirm ETA assuming expedited handling. Also please attach the sample manifest/playbook mentioned earlier.

Regards,

Audrey

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Audrey Li <audrey.li@finvest.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit log extract — legal-hold slice & residency boundary questions

Audrey — agreed on all points. Attached: export_playbook_v1.pdf (short playbook), audit_manifest_sample.csv (sample manifest format), md5_checksums.txt (example checksum output). Quick answers inline then logistics.

1) Manifest fields: export_uuid, file_name, byte_size, sha256_checksum, original_event_utc_ts_min, original_event_utc_ts_max, export_generation_ts_utc, operator_id, tenant_id, region_tag. We will provide a PGP-signed manifest and system signature.

2) Retention on Redwood side: we can commit contractually to a 7-day retention maximum for the exported bundle following successful transfer and verification. We will provide a signed deletion attestation (contains export_uuid, deletion_ts_utc, deleted_by_sys_id). If you want a shorter window (e.g., 48 hours) we can accommodate in the SOW.

3) Residency determination: primary is tenant residency flag (how the tenant is configured for data residency). For traffic where tenant residency is ambiguous (cross-border access), our export filter includes events that are tagged by the data-plane region in which the event was recorded; we do not rely solely on ephemeral source IP geolocation unless the tenant requests that filter. We'll include a field in the manifest that notes "residency_basis" with one of [tenant_flag, data_plane_region, source_ip_geolocation] and the method used.

4) Timestamp fidelity: original UTC timestamps are preserved. If any normalization is applied (e.g., ingest-time correction), the manifest will include a normalization_flag and notes.

ETA for expedited S3 push for the requested window (finvest-prod-47, Apr 2027): assuming expedited, target 48–72 hours from SOW acceptance and access to the target bucket (we need an IAM role or pre-signed temp creds). Volume estimate (approx): 120GB compressed — nominal. If that looks right, please share the S3 bucket details and whether Redwood should assume responsibility to upload direct or if a pre-signed URL is preferred.

We will:
- Generate export bundle(s) segmented by day, produce manifest.csv with SHA256 checksums, PGP-sign the manifest, and upload to your S3 bucket.
- Retain copies for 7 days by default, delete thereafter and produce deletion attestation.
- Provide chain-of-custody PDF and a contact for 24x7 export escalation (marissa.cole@redwood.com).

Attachments:
- export_playbook_v1.pdf (Export flow, roles, verification checklist)
- audit_manifest_sample.csv (columns and sample rows)
- md5_checksums.txt (legacy compatibility; primary is SHA256 in the manifest)

Let us know bucket details and if you want the 7-day retention or 48-hour. Once we have access we can schedule the expedited run.

Best,

Markus
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
